description:
Repository-image captures for mutations, repairs and proposed-state validation read every document referenced by any issue, in full, so they grow with project history and `jit recover` fails on a repository with large referenced documents. Document bytes are read only where a pass consumes them.

## Background

`capture_proposed_base` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:183-206`) grows its base through `grow_discovering(.., discover_document_references)` (`validate.rs:890-903`). For every document reference on every issue, this requests the working-tree file and the pinned git blob. The base serves `repair_derived_state` (`jit recover`, `claim.rs:720`, `validate.rs:554`), proposed-state validation (`validate.rs:161`), `config set` (`config.rs:265`), `init` (`init.rs:211,245,1347`) and `gate check` (`gate_check.rs:818`), all under `CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB, `commands/mod.rs:269`).

Observed in a downstream repository, where both `jit recover` and `jit validate` fail (copy reproduced with the installed 1.0.0 binary and with main at 01c3d8f85): `jit recover` fails with `captured 537290260 bytes but the maximum is 536870912`. The repository has 4318 document references to 4037 unique paths (bench logs and receipts up to 60 MB). The capture reads about 269 MB of working-tree files plus 267 MB of pinned blobs. The `.jit` data itself is about 6 MB of that.

This contradicts `@/charter/D-19`: reads never scale with project history.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit recover` and derived-state repair capture no document-reference content, and succeed on a repository whose referenced documents total more than the capture byte budget.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every capture that serves a mutation (`config set`, `init`, `gate check`, issue mutations) reads document-reference content only for the documents a pass of that mutation consumes, never every issue's documents.
- [hard] REQ-03: `jit validate` succeeds on a repository whose referenced documents total more than the capture byte budget, and its document-reference checks keep their current verdicts: a missing, changed or dangling document reference is still reported.
- [hard] REQ-04: One owning test proves that a derived-state repair over an issue whose referenced document exceeds a small capture budget succeeds without reading it, and one owning test proves REQ-02's per-mutation scoping at the shared capture mechanism.
title: Mutation and repair captures read only the documents their passes consume
